take: Brent touching nearly $110 on Thursday for the first time since July, with the IRGC confirming an attack on shipping infrastructure and StanChart warning that oil is now built for sharper, more frequent spikes, is the story that matters most for crude and products alike. The second theme is the Strait of Hormuz risk premium bleeding into freight, with the Splash Wrap noting how quickly shipping risk was repriced and Black Sea drifting drone discoveries up 208% in six months, whilst the Saudis and US plan action against Houthi aggression at Bab el-Mandeb. On flows, the EIA has US crude production averaging a record 13.8m b/d in 2026, which caps the upside from supply shocks but does nothing for the product side where elevated crack spreads are already feeding through to the pump. The cross-market link to watch is bunker versus gasoil: with Hormuz headlines driving crude and LNG bunkering expanding at Tenerife and Ulsan, the refining margin and the bunker curve are the cleanest read on whether this is a genuine supply event or a positioning squeeze. In the next 24 hours, watch whether the Fed hike odds that rekindled recession fears actually crystallise, and whether the Hormuz plan produces a de-escalation headline or a Houthi response that pushes Brent through $110 with product cracks following.
